release.name: hato 1.0.3
release.body:
**Japanese subtitles for your Japanese video. Found, matched, and timed — without you doing anything.**

This release answers two reports from people using 1.0.2: hato fetched `.ass` where `.srt` was wanted, and it fetched subtitles for videos that already had them.

---

## New

**Choose `.ass` or `.srt`.** Settings → **Subtitle format**. hato downloads the kind you prefer, and the other kind only if you tick *"If there is no .ass, download .srt or another format"*. The box starts off.

**An episode jimaku has only in the other format says so.** It waits in **Needs you** as *"only as .srt on jimaku"*, with **Download .srt instead** — one click ticks the box and fetches it.

## Fixed

**It fetched subtitles for videos that already had them.**

- A subtitle named exactly like the video, with no language in its name — `Show - 01.srt` beside `Show - 01.mkv` — is now **read**. If its text is clearly Japanese, hato leaves the video alone and says why. If it can't tell (too short, mixed with another language, an encoding it can't read), it fetches, as before.
- `Show - 01.jp.srt` counts as Japanese. `jp` is Japan's country code rather than a language code, but plenty of files use it. This comes from tsubasa 0.1.8.

**A download that failed was reported as a timing mismatch**, and the episode set aside for a day. It is an error now, and the next run tries again.

**A film jimaku has only as an archive was offered the archive as its subtitle.** It isn't any more.

**With archives turned on, an archive was downloaded again at every retry.** One already downloaded is reused, and one holding the format you prefer is opened even when plain files of the other format sit beside it.

And about twenty smaller things, found by an adversarial review of this release before it went out.

---

## Upgrading from 1.0.2

Unzip 1.0.3 and run **`hato.exe`**. Your settings, key and history carry over.

- **With the default setting, an episode jimaku has only as `.srt` is no longer downloaded.** It waits in *Needs you* with **Download .srt instead**. To have hato take whatever format is there, tick the box in Settings → Subtitle format.
- **If hato is in your tray, restart it before you change the format setting.** A tray from an older hato cannot read the setting, and the runs it starts stop until it is restarted. Once you change it, Settings says so beside the setting, with a **Restart the tray** button.
- **If you turned on the daily run or *Start with Windows* and put 1.0.3 in a different folder**, switch them off and on so they point at the new one. Settings says so when they point somewhere else.

## Windows — download and run

Download **`hato-1.0.3-windows-x64.zip`** below, unzip it anywhere, and run **`hato.exe`**.

Nothing to install. Python is already inside it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `hato.exe` | the window — the one file you click |
| `hato-cli.exe` | the command line |
| `hato-watch.exe` | the tray watcher, and what the daily run starts |

You'll need a free API key from your jimaku.cc account. Open **Settings → Jimaku key**, paste it, and hato tests it there and tells you whether it works.

## Any platform — from source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SonicSandbox/hato
cd hato
pip install "tsubasa-sync[parsing]>=0.1.8" requests
python -m hato ~/Anime/Some\ Show
```

Python 3.10+. Add `pip install "PyQt6>=6.5"` for the window, then `python -m hato.gui`.

---

## What hato does

**Works out what the video is** — not by folder names or `SxxExx`. It reads the filename the way a person does: release group, season, episode, romanised or Japanese title.

**Finds the subtitle that goes with *your* copy.** There are usually several. It picks by which release it came from and tries the next one if the first does not fit.

**Times it to your exact file.** A subtitle written for a different release is seconds out — sometimes minutes, sometimes drifting scene by scene. hato hands it to [tsubasa](https://pypi.org/project/tsubasa-sync/), which re-times it and **refuses to write anything it cannot verify**.

**Keeps watching.** About 31 MB resident in the tray, measured on this release's own bytes. A new episode lands, hato waits a minute for the download to finish, then goes and gets the subtitle.

**Asks when it isn't sure** — and says what it is waiting for when it is.

---

## What it will not do

- Write anything it isn't sure about
- Leave scratch files in your media folder
- Delete your files
- Re-encode or convert a subtitle — `.ass` stays `.ass`, in its original encoding
- Redistribute anything. Subtitles are downloaded to your machine, at your request

---

## Notes

The Windows build is unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn you about an unknown publisher on first run.

For a season still airing, the subtitle is usually published hours to days *after* the episode — hato says *probably not out yet* when that is what it sees, and looks again a day later: on its own while the tray or the daily run is on, and otherwise the next time it runs.

GPL-3.0-or-later. `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` are inside the zip, and `packaging/` in this repository is its Corresponding Source.
